scope: Research only. Same-utterance Local256 lifted to 512, Base512 and active Gap512; preserve OSRAM read/write query, Flat and task loss. No extra data, cache, imputation, auxiliary loss or gold labels.
shortfall: 本lane未凑足14个新方法。现13项是筛选记录：2项可迁移研究设计、4项条件候选、7项拒绝；拒绝项不能计入新增名额。最新40合适迁移补查增加PO和完整RepSet；PSWE作者实现化简后与已有FSPool过近，拒绝计新。admissible仅表示完整计算机制可按当前输入/损失约束迁移，不表示实现已验证或性能提升。
source_policy: Paper method sections and the named author code files were accessed on the survey date. Mutable branch URLs are not version-pinned; only listed files/functions were inspected, not full repositories or runtime behavior. All OSRAM benefits and mappings below are research hypotheses rather than source-paper results.

implementation_handoff.input_contract: One utterance only: Local [256], Base [512], Gap [3,512] and active Gap mask. Form X [N,512], N<=5, using learned Local-to-512 lift and known role embeddings. Roles are whole vectors, never split into head tokens. Pack absent Gap roles out; preserve existing history/no-op guards externally.
chain: Compute shared two-layer pair comparator f([x_i,x_j]); C_ij=f([x_i,x_j])-f([x_j,x_i]), yielding antisymmetric C [N,N]. Normalize C by Frobenius norm with explicit zero-norm guard as in root permutation.py.
Initialize permutation logits U [N,N] to zeros (source PO-U). Rows identify input roles; columns identify computational sequence positions. This is not physical or utterance time.

For each source-style unrolled iteration: P=Sinkhorn(U), where source root sinkhorn first uses row softmax(U/temperature), then four alternating row/column normalizations. Use finite source normalization, not a claim of exact doubly stochasticity.

Compute B_jq=sum_{k>q}P_jk-sum_{k<q}P_jk and G=2*C*B by matrix multiplication. Update U=U-abs(learned_step)*G. Do not multiply this inner update by the Sinkhorn Jacobian: Eq.7 and source implement the alternate gradient. Outer backprop still differentiates the unrolled tensor computation.
Apply final Sinkhorn to U and form ordered complete-role vectors Y=P^T X [N,512]. The shared order must apply to all channels; do not sort channels independently.

Encode Y with an LSTM and use final cell state c_N, matching ban-vqa/permnet.py; project c_N with existing role-aware residual/output conventions back into the original role-aligned slots. Do not hand Flat reordered slots.
Train comparator, step size and sequence encoder through existing task loss only. No target ordering, VQA box features, auxiliary optimization penalty or restored BAN model is introduced.
implementation_handoff.source_vs_adapter_boundary: Pair comparator, normalized pair cost, relaxed-order objective gradient, unrolled alternate updates, assignment application and LSTM cell readout are source mechanisms. Whole OSRAM role input and role-aware final correction decoder are interface adaptations. The VQA-specific boxes/attention features are not intrinsic requirements of the generic PO method.
future_checks: Input role permutation with attached IDs leaves c_N invariant within numerical tolerance
Inactive Gap perturbation has no effect
Joint channel ordering, correct P transpose
Task-only gradients reach comparator and LSTM
Do not claim exact combinatorial optimum from finite unrolled iterations

methods.title: Learning Representations of Sets through Optimized Permutations

source_evidence.paper: Sections 2.1-2.3 Eqs.1-8 define antisymmetric pairwise costs, quadratic ordering objective, relaxed permutation and unrolled optimization. Eq.7 specifically updates logits using the gradient with respect to normalized P; Appendix D explains omitting the Sinkhorn Jacobian in that inner update. Introduction and VQA experiment permit implicit task supervision.
source_evidence.code: permutation.py::Comparator, assignment_grad, calculate_assignment, sinkhorn and apply_assignment were read in full. ban-vqa/permnet.py::PermNet.forward computes pairwise skew, optimized assignment, applies it, and returns the LSTM cell state. The corresponding ban-vqa/permutation.py was also read.
source_evidence.access_limit: arXiv HTML failed; 26-page full PDF succeeded. No code execution or training.

methods.mechanism: Learn an antisymmetric precedence cost; optimize a whole relaxed permutation against pairwise ordering consistency; encode the canonically ordered feature sequence with an LSTM.
methods.osram_mapping: Pack at most five currently available vectors: projected Local256, Base512 and active Gap512. Role identity travels with each vector. Optimize an N-by-N assignment only within this utterance, encode its ordered 512-dimensional vectors, then decode role-aware corrections to the existing Flat slots. Preserve original query/read/write and task loss; no boxes, temporal coordinates, permutation labels or auxiliary loss.
methods.substantive_difference: FSPool independently ranks channels; Janossy averages all orderings. PO learns one global vector ordering from pairwise precedence and optimizes it inside forward. OTKE solves fixed linear-cost support transport and emits barycentric features; PO solves a quadratic ordering objective then sequentially encodes it. Prior graph matching uses soft cross-graph residuals/GRUs, not global precedence optimization. PointCNN predicts a transform directly, not this optimization chain.
methods.expected_benefit_hypothesis: May learn an evidence-processing order that preserves interactions among five complete roles better than immediate pooling.
risks: Use the source alternate inner gradient update; replacing it with arbitrary differentiable sorting is a different method.
Soft assignment may blend roles; keep role identities and original residual paths.
No claim of an actual temporal sequence; the order is task-learned computational precedence.
Comparator ties, zero norm and packed cardinalities need numerical tests when implemented.

implementation_handoff.input_contract: Pack whole current role vectors X [N,512], N<=5, with Local lifted from256 and role identities attached. Learned hidden sets H [K,5,512] are parameters, not data caches.
chain: For each hidden set k, compute S_k=ReLU(X H_k^T) [N,5]. Preserve source ReLU inner-product affinity.

Solve exact max sum_i S_k[i,pi(i)] over injections pi from N observed roles into five reference elements. N<=5 gives at most 120 assignments. Because S>=0 and five supports are at least N, extending any partial matching to an injection cannot lower its value; this attains the source at-most-one-per-row/column objective without invented observations.

Use the maximized score divided by N, as the author code does, as the kth component of z [K]. Gather winning scores so task gradients flow through actual selected affinities; assignments are piecewise constant and ties use an explicit deterministic subgradient policy.

Project the template-score vector with the parent-approved existing role-output adapter into original Flat input slots, retaining old OSRAM query/read/write and task loss. Do not replace scores with matched/support-pooled feature vectors.
implementation_handoff.source_vs_adapter_boundary: Learned hidden sets, ReLU affinity, two-sided one-to-one capacities, maximum objective score representation and per-input-count normalization follow the author method/code. Bounded enumeration is a solver replacement that computes the same optimum at this small N; it is not a separately counted method. Role-aware output reconstruction is the OSRAM adapter only.
future_checks: Compare tiny enumerated cases with hand-computed optimal matching scores
Row and reference-set element permutation invariance
One role cannot occupy two template elements
Mask before matching and normalize by actual N
No OTKE/Sinkhorn shortcut or ApproxRepSet one-sided constraint relaxation

methods.title: Rep the Set: Neural Networks for Learning Set Representations

source_evidence.paper: Section 3 Eq.1 imposes at-most-one row and column capacities on nonnegative matching variables; Figure 2 represents a set by optimal matching objective values against several learned hidden sets. Eqs.2-5 derive gradients using optimal assignments. ApproxRepSet removes one capacity constraint and is not the proposed transfer.
source_evidence.code: repset/models.py::RepSet.train/test form ReLU(W dot x), call lapjv(-K, extend_cost=True), retain assignment D and normalized objective -cost/|X|; train computes manual hidden-set gradients. Entire 103-line author file read.
source_evidence.access_limit: Original is NumPy with manual training and lapjv, not a verified PyTorch layer. Its manual updates should not be copied as an autograd implementation.

methods.mechanism: Represent the complete role set by exact maximum-weight one-to-one partial matching scores against a bank of learned multi-element reference sets.
methods.osram_mapping: Use at most five active role vectors, each carrying its known role ID, and learned reference sets of at most five elements. ReLU inner-product affinities plus exact capacity-constrained matching yield one score per template; project the score vector into existing 512-dimensional Flat corrections. At this size assignments can be exhaustively evaluated (at most 5! full assignments when padded with zero-score dummies), retaining selected-score gradients without installing a solver. This is a design proposal only; no implementation was performed.
methods.substantive_difference: The novelty is the bank of capacity-constrained set-template objective scores, not replacing Sinkhorn with a hard solver. OTKE transports all mass and outputs support-wise weighted feature vectors; RepSet can leave elements unmatched and emits each entire template's optimal objective. Historical graph matching updates observed Base/Gap states through soft attention; no learned template-bank objective layer exists. NetVLAD residual sums and slots also lack one-to-one template capacity.
methods.expected_benefit_hypothesis: May recognize combinations of complementary role evidence while preventing one strong role from satisfying every element of a template.
risks: Retain exact two-sided capacity constraints and template-score output; soft transport pooling would duplicate OTKE.
Small sets can overfit template banks; more templates are a hyperparameter, not further methods.
Matching ties give subgradients; zero affinities and role masking need explicit tests.
Learned references are model parameters, not a cache of other utterances.

methods.title: Pooling by Sliced-Wasserstein Embedding

source_evidence.paper: Section 4 Eq.7 constructs one-dimensional Monge maps through quantile functions; Section 2 explicitly relates PSWE to FSPool and introduces learned slicers/reference sets. Read full PDF method rather than abstract only.
source_evidence.code: pswe.py::PSWE.forward was read in full: normalized linear slicer, per-slice sort, optional Interp1d to reference cardinality, reference-order gather, reference-minus-quantile residual and linear weighted sum. get_slice is self.theta(X).
source_evidence.prior_code: gcnet_missing_m3/meaningful_input_sorting.py::FeaturewiseSortPool and SortPoolUnpoolCore already provide tokenwise learned transforms, rank-weighted feature sorting and downstream latent transforms.

methods.mechanism: Sliced quantile transport embedding, compressed by learned linear weights over reference points.
methods.osram_mapping: It could pool the active five-role set without physical coordinates, but feasibility is not novelty. Retaining role-wise quantile correspondence would require a new design, not automatically the author pooling code.
methods.substantive_difference: Different from OTKE's multivariate balanced Sinkhorn barycentric pooling, yet too close to FSPool: for a fixed learned reference ordering, author output y_j=sum_m w_jm*r_mj-sum_m w_jm*sorted(theta X)_{p_m,j}. Thus reference subtraction is a constant offset and p merely permutes learned rank weights. Interpolation and slicer projection do not by themselves establish a distinct core. This algebraic assessment is our inference from inspected code.
methods.expected_benefit_hypothesis: Distributional interpretation may aid design, but no new expressivity beyond the existing rank-pooling family is established here.
risks: Do not claim the final compressed weighted vector retains the full pre-compression sliced-Wasserstein isometry.
Using nonlinear slicers or retaining a larger quantile vector is not enough to count another candidate without a separately justified complete mechanism.
Inactive roles must be excluded rather than padded into the empirical distribution.

methods.title: MagNet: A Neural Network for Directed Graphs

source_evidence.paper: Author-hosted full PDF Sections 2-3: A_s=(A+A^T)/2, Theta=2*pi*q*(A-A^T), H=A_s*exp(i*Theta), normalized Hermitian Laplacian and complex Chebyshev network. q=0 loses direction.
source_evidence.code: src/utils/hermitian.py::decomp and hermitian_decomp_sparse construct antisymmetric phase and normalized magnetic Laplacian; src/layer/sparse_magnet.py::process mixes real/imaginary parts with complex multiplication, ChebConv.forward sums polynomial terms, complex_relu_layer gates both parts by real-part sign. Both actual files were read through HTTPS.
source_evidence.access_limit: PMC blocked; author PDF succeeded. Reference preprocessing uses NumPy/SciPy and static operators, so learned per-example graph gradients are not provided by this code.

methods.mechanism: Direction-dependent phase transport with coupled real/imaginary states across nonlinear magnetic spectral layers.
methods.osram_mapping: Infer nonnegative directed relations from current active role pairs using distinct sender/receiver projections, or justify directions by existing role semantics. Construct per-example Hermitian operators without caching; retain complex state until the final real 512 projection before Flat. Preserve OSRAM query/task loss.
methods.substantive_difference: Old real symmetric filtering discards A-A^T. MagNet preserves it as orientation phase and transports coupled real/imaginary states; changing polynomial basis alone does not count. Diagonal real sheaf restrictions are not this magnetic connection. q=0 or early imaginary-part deletion disqualifies the design.
methods.expected_benefit_hypothesis: May distinguish asymmetric Base-to-Gap versus Gap-to-Base influence without invented spatial coordinates.
risks: Relation direction is hypothesized or learned, not an observed causal edge.
Symmetric learned A collapses to an old undirected spectral family.
Differentiable per-utterance operator construction requires an independent adaptation of static preprocessing.
Only the full complex nonlinear chain qualifies; a Laplacian swap alone is insufficient.

methods.title: Signed Graph Convolutional Networks

source_evidence.paper: Section II.B Eq.1 defines balanced/unbalanced path recursion; II.C Eqs.2-5 maintain two states with positive-edge same-state propagation and negative-edge cross-state propagation. II.D supplies the original signed-network objective, which is not proposed for transfer.
source_evidence.code: Author archive linked by https://tylersnetwork.github.io/publications.html was downloaded in memory and inspected: Signed_Graph_Convolutional_Networks/SGCN/aggregators.py::NonFirstLayerAggregator.forward forms [A+H_B,A-H_U,H_B] and [A+H_U,A-H_B,H_U]; encoders.py::LayerEncoder uses distinct weight_bal/weight_unbal followed by tanh.
source_evidence.access_limit: Old MSU ZIP URL returned non-ZIP content; author's current GitHub Pages ZIP succeeded. The separately linked benedekrozemberczki implementation was correctly treated as third-party, not original author code.

methods.mechanism: Separate representations summarize paths with even versus odd numbers of negative relations, and negative edges exchange the two channels at each composition step.
methods.osram_mapping: Build a signed relation graph only from active same-utterance role content, then retain both parity states through at least two propagation steps and project their concatenation to 512 before Flat. Use existing task loss only, with no link-sign labels or the source embedding/triplet objective. Discrete signs need a justified content-only rule; a learned soft-sign relaxation would be an explicit adaptation.
methods.substantive_difference: Positive gates and generic recurrent messages do not enforce path parity. Differential attention subtracts two maps once; SGCN maintains two states and cross-routes them recursively so two negative steps return to the balanced channel. This is not simply negative attention weights.
methods.expected_benefit_hypothesis: May separate direct disagreement from agreement reached through an even number of conflicting relations.
risks: Balance theory on social friends/foes is not established for modality evidence.
No observed signed edges are provided; cosine sign is not automatically agreement or contradiction.
A soft weighted relaxation must retain the full parity recurrence and be labeled as adaptation.
One layer or two independent positive/negative GCNs would remove the distinguishing cross-state mechanism.

methods.title: Topological Graph Neural Networks

source_evidence.paper: Section 4 defines learned vertex filtrations, edge filtration max(f(u),f(v)), persistent pairing, vertex-associated H0 embeddings and graph-pooled H1 embeddings. Section 4.2 Theorem 1 requires distinct vertex filtration values for local differentiability.
source_evidence.code: topognn/layers.py::SimpleSetTopoLayer.compute_persistence calls compute_persistence_homology_batched_mt after max endpoint filtration; forward restores per-vertex H0 features and pools nonzero H1 pairs. Inspected actual source including fake_persistence_computation; fake mode is an ablation and must be disabled.
source_evidence.access_limit: OpenReview was challenge-blocked; arXiv full HTML supplied the method. C++ persistence backend was not inspected.

methods.mechanism: Learn task-dependent filtration values, compute actual birth/death pairings, embed global persistence relationships and return vertex-aligned features.
methods.osram_mapping: Treat existing role vectors as attributed vertices of a semantic incidence graph, with edges justified by Base/Gap role relations rather than spatial locations. Exclude inactive Gap vertices before pairing. Preserve query and Flat; use only task loss for filtration learning. Mapping remains conditional on a nondegenerate, justified graph definition.
methods.substantive_difference: Actual filtration-induced persistence pairing is absent from Hodge diffusion, cellular incidence propagation, restriction-map diffusion and scattering; it is not merely an additional simplicial layer.
methods.expected_benefit_hypothesis: May capture whether role evidence forms robust connected groups across learned thresholds.
risks: A complete role graph with lower-star filtration can make H0 mostly zero-persistence and erase the proposed benefit.
Very few vertices and fixed incidence can collapse topology to cardinality or order statistics.
No invented A/T/V coordinates. Graph choice, tie policy, gradients and inactive-role handling remain unresolved.
No new dependency is authorized; reference backend compatibility is unverified.

methods.title: Sign and Basis Invariant Networks for Spectral Graph Representation Learning

source_evidence.paper: Section 2, Eq.3 and Eq.5 use phi(v)+phi(-v); Eq.4 processes VV^T with IGN; Section 2.2 composes eigenspaces and includes eigenvalues/features in Eq.6. Section 3.1 distinguishes this family from spectral graph convolution.
source_evidence.code: LearningFilters/signbasisnet.py::SignPlus.forward evaluates shared model(v)+model(-v), retaining x without sign flip; IGNBasisInv.forward dispatches projector encoders by eigenspace multiplicity. Actual 59-line raw file was read.
source_evidence.access_limit: IGN2to1 implementation and full eigendecomposition/preprocessing path were not audited.

methods.mechanism: Nonlinear spectral encoding respecting independent eigenvector sign ambiguity and orthogonal basis changes within repeated eigenspaces; count the paper family once.
methods.osram_mapping: Build a symmetric relation matrix solely from active same-utterance roles, obtain its eigenvectors/eigenspaces, encode spectral quotients jointly with role content and return 512-dimensional corrections before Flat. Spectral coordinates are derived from observed relations, not assigned spatial positions.
methods.substantive_difference: Bernstein filters apply a polynomial operator to features. Grassmann pooling summarizes feature subspaces. This candidate instead nonlinearly encodes each role-relation eigenspace modulo its basis symmetry. Merely pooling VV^T would duplicate Grassmann and is excluded; SignNet/BasisNet are not counted separately.
methods.expected_benefit_hypothesis: May expose evidence-cluster structure with stable sign handling beyond a fixed spectral filter.
risks: Fixed complete unweighted role graphs produce repeated/constant spectra and nearly useless encodings.
SignNet alone does not resolve repeated-eigenvalue basis ambiguity.
Eigenvalue crossings, eigenspace grouping and backpropagation require explicit numerical treatment.
Strong prior overlap means full nonlinear quotient encoding must survive implementation; projector pooling alone is rejected.

methods.title: PersLay: A Neural Network Layer for Persistence Diagrams and New Graph Topological Signatures

source_evidence.paper: Sections 2.1/2.2 define extended persistence and heat-kernel signature; Section 3.1 Eq.4 defines weighted point transformation followed by invariant aggregation.
source_evidence.code: perslay/perslay.py::compute_representations constructs weights, applies diagram transforms, mask and invariant pooling; call concatenates diagram representations with features before rho. Actual code body inspected.

methods.mechanism: Extended persistence encodes ordinary and relative components/cycles, then learns diagram vectorization.
methods.osram_mapping: Could compute diagrams on same-utterance role relations and feed their encoding to Flat, but static complete graphs give content-independent HKS signatures.
methods.substantive_difference: Extended persistence differs mathematically from ordinary persistence; nevertheless, on the current tiny role structure the justified transfer has not demonstrated a core beyond the same persistence-pairing family. Do not count it as a second TOGL slot.
methods.expected_benefit_hypothesis: Potentially describes persistent role relationships, unestablished here.
risks: High within-survey overlap with TOGL.
Fixed structural HKS may ignore sample content.
Reference legacy TensorFlow code does not provide verified differentiable construction from OSRAM features.

methods.title: Geometric Algebra Transformer

source_evidence.paper: Full NeurIPS PDF accessed; geometric representations and E(3)-equivariant architecture use projective geometric algebra for geometric objects.
source_evidence.code: gatr/primitives/bilinear.py::geometric_product and outer_product contract explicit 16x16x16 multiplication tensors with multivectors; source inspected.
source_evidence.access_limit: Only bilinear primitives inspected, not every complete transformer layer.

methods.mechanism: Projective multivectors combine geometric objects through structured products inside an E(3)-equivariant transformer.
methods.osram_mapping: Rejected: Local/Base/Gap embeddings have no justified point, plane, line or transformation semantics. Arbitrary packing into multivector coefficients does not establish the required geometric group action.
methods.substantive_difference: Geometric multiplication and representation constraints differ from relation attention and pair composition, but the actual geometric semantics do not transfer.
methods.expected_benefit_hypothesis: Only a speculative structured-interaction bias remains; insufficient for admission.
risks: Artificial geometry and unsupported equivariance claims.
Using only the algebraic product degenerates to a structured bilinear primitive, which the user rejects.

methods.title: E(n) Equivariant Graph Neural Networks

source_evidence.paper: ICML PDF method uses invariant squared distances and equivariant relative-coordinate updates alongside hidden-feature updates.
source_evidence.code: models/gcl.py::E_GCL.coord2radial computes coordinate differences and squared norms; coord_model aggregates difference times edge-conditioned scalar; forward updates both coordinates and features.

methods.mechanism: Joint invariant message passing and equivariant coordinate dynamics.
methods.osram_mapping: Rejected under present semantics. Treating arbitrary 512-dimensional embeddings as coordinates can be algebraically executable, but no basis/translation symmetry of the upstream representations is established.
methods.substantive_difference: Coordinate evolution is genuinely different from EdgeConv, but deleting it leaves another endpoint-conditioned message network; inventing coordinates does not validate the retained mechanism.
methods.expected_benefit_hypothesis: Latent-distance refinement is speculative and not evidence for geometric equivariance benefit.
risks: Modality channels have learned semantic meaning; arbitrary rotations need not preserve their meaning.
No justified latent coordinate action or physical geometry.

methods.title: Vector Neurons: A General Framework for SO(3)-Equivariant Networks

source_evidence.paper: Section 3 introduces 3D-vector channels, shared linear maps and equivariant directional nonlinearities, with invariant readout.
source_evidence.code: models/vn_layers.py::VNLinearLeakyReLU uses feature and direction maps with VNBatchNorm; actual raw author source inspected.
source_evidence.access_limit: CVF PDF request failed; Stanford author-hosted full PDF succeeded.

methods.mechanism: Vector-valued neuron operations preserve simultaneous SO(3) rotations.
methods.osram_mapping: Rejected: partitioning 512 learned channels into triples or labeling A/T/V as x/y/z invents a rotation representation. No such transformation is part of OSRAM evidence semantics.
methods.substantive_difference: SO(3)-equivariant nonlinear feature types differ from learned neighborhood transforms, but cannot justify a new applicable method without real vector semantics.
methods.expected_benefit_hypothesis: Parameter sharing might regularize but this is neither established nor a sufficient substantive method claim.
risks: Arbitrary channel grouping.
Operator-only substitution prohibited by the current screening criteria.

methods.title: LieTransformer: Equivariant Self-Attention for Lie Groups

source_evidence.paper: Section 3.1 Eq.5 lifts spatial inputs to cosets s(x)H; Section 3.2 Algorithm 1 combines content kernel and relative-group kernel k_l(g^-1 g'). Equivariance requires a homogeneous input space.
source_evidence.code: eqv_transformer/eqv_attention.py::EquivariantTransformer.forward calls group.lift; EquivairantMultiheadAttention extracts group neighborhoods and computes normalized kernel weights. Actual source accessed; symbol spelling follows author code.

methods.mechanism: Coset lifting, relative-group attention and invariant group pooling.
methods.osram_mapping: Rejected: role identities are typed semantic evidence, not samples on a specified homogeneous Lie-group space. Ordinary token permutation is already covered by prior set models and Janossy symmetrization.
methods.substantive_difference: Coset lifting is not ordinary attention, but its extra information is absent. Recasting role permutations as the new contribution would repeat prior symmetrization.
methods.expected_benefit_hypothesis: No justified new invariance benefit for the available inputs.
risks: Unspecified group action and homogeneous-space assumption.
Stochastic group lifting adds cost without supporting geometry.

methods.title: Gauge Equivariant Mesh CNNs: Anisotropic Convolutions on Geometric Graphs

source_evidence.paper: Sections 2 and 3.2 require a geometric mesh, local tangent directions and parallel edge transport; Section 3.1 constrains anisotropic kernels by gauge equivariance.
source_evidence.code: gem_cnn/nn/gem_conv.py::GemConv.message applies rep_act using angle_pre, contracts radial_weights with kernels, then applies angle_post. Entire source file inspected.

methods.mechanism: Anisotropic convolution with local-frame gauge constraints and parallel transport of geometric feature representations.
methods.osram_mapping: Rejected: a Local/Base/Gap role set does not supply a mesh, tangent planes, edge angles or a geometric connection. Learned arbitrary maps would move back toward prior sheaf diffusion without the source geometry.
methods.substantive_difference: Geometric parallel transport differs from learned incidence maps only while the manifold/connection assumptions are retained; those assumptions are absent here.
methods.expected_benefit_hypothesis: No supported transport-based benefit on the specified role vectors.
risks: Invented tangent geometry.
Replacing transport with unconstrained learned maps would duplicate an existing family.
